notes.summary: Current Affairs gives 2–4 questions, usually on events of the last 6–12 months. This app does not carry monthly news — take that from a reliable external source (a monthly current-affairs compilation, PIB releases, a national newspaper). What this topic covers is the stable background that every news question leans on: which body publishes which index or report, and where international organisations are headquartered.

concepts.title: How to study current affairs
concepts.body:
• Use one monthly compilation from a trusted source; revise the last 12 months before the exam.
  • Make short notes under fixed heads: appointments, awards, sports, summits, schemes, indices and rankings, defence exercises, obituaries, science.
  • For every index in the news, note three things: publisher, India's rank, the top country. Ranks change every year; the publisher does not — learn that here.
  • For every summit, note the host city and country and link the organisation to its HQ from the table below.
  • Revise with flashcards weekly; old months fade fast.

varieties.name: Index ↔ publisher
varieties.how: Recall the publisher table. In a news question, the rank changes each year but the publisher is fixed.

example.q: The Global Gender Gap Report is published by:
steps: Gender Gap, Global Risks → World Economic Forum

varieties.name: Organisation ↔ headquarters
varieties.how: Group by city: Geneva (WHO, ILO, WTO), Vienna (IAEA, OPEC), Washington (IMF, World Bank).

example.q: Where is the headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency?
steps: IAEA and OPEC are both in Vienna

varieties.name: Indian reports and data
varieties.how: Link each regular report to the ministry or body that releases it.

example.q: Who releases the India State of Forest Report?
steps: By the Forest Survey of India (Ministry of Environment)

tips: Monthly news is not in this app — use one trusted external monthly source and revise the last 12 months.
WEF publishes the Gender Gap and Global Risks reports; its annual meeting is at Davos.
Geneva hosts the most UN-linked bodies: WHO, ILO, WTO (WTO is not a UN agency but sits there too).
traps: UNESCO is in Paris, but UNICEF is in New York.
IMF and World Bank are both in Washington, D.C., not New York.
World Happiness Report is not published by WHO or UNDP.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO)?
questions.solution:
WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
Memory hook: Geneva = 'Gene' = health.

questions.q: The Human Development Index (HDI) is published by:
questions.solution:
HDI appears in the Human Development Report of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
Memory hook: Human Development — UNDP.

questions.q: The Economic Survey of India is presented by which ministry?
questions.solution:
The Economic Survey is prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, and presented before the Union Budget.
Memory hook: Survey before Budget — both from the Finance Ministry.

questions.q: The World Press Freedom Index is released by:
questions.solution:
The World Press Freedom Index is published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), based in Paris. Transparency International publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index.
Memory hook: Press = Reporters.

questions.q: Which pair of organisations both have their headquarters in Vienna?
questions.solution:
IAEA and OPEC are in Vienna. ILO and WTO are in Geneva; IMF and World Bank in Washington, D.C.; UNESCO and OECD in Paris.
Memory hook: Vienna runs on Atoms and Oil.

questions.q: The Global Innovation Index is published by:
questions.solution:
The Global Innovation Index is published by WIPO, a UN agency based in Geneva.
Memory hook: Innovation → patents → intellectual property → WIPO.

The New Development Bank (set up by BRICS) is headquartered in Shanghai. Beijing hosts the AIIB.
Memory hook: BRICS bank by the sea — Shanghai; AIIB in the capital — Beijing.

questions.q: Which of the following is released by the National Statistics Office (MoSPI)?
questions.solution:
NSO releases the IIP, CPI and the Periodic Labour Force Survey. WPI comes from DPIIT, the Financial Stability Report from RBI, and the forest report from the Forest Survey of India.
Memory hook: Statistics Office counts output, prices for consumers, and jobs.
